facts: Bruny Island consists of two landmasses connected by a narrow sandy isthmus called The Neck.
The Neck Reserve is a famous rookery for little penguins and short-tailed shearwaters returning at dusk.
The island was named after French explorer Bruni d'Entrecasteaux, who surveyed the area in 1792.
Indigenous Nuenonne people lived on the island for thousands of years before European settlement.
Bruny Island is famous for fresh local oysters harvested directly from the pristine surrounding coastal waters.
Artisanal cheesemakers on the island produce award-winning cheeses using traditional hand-crafted methods.
Cape Bruny Lighthouse is Australia's second-oldest continuously manned lighthouse, built by convicts in 1836.
South Bruny National Park features lush temperate rainforests filled with ancient tree ferns and giant eucalyptus trees.
Rare albino Bennett's wallabies live freely in the wild across the northern parts of the island.
Every year runners compete in a challenging fifty-kilometer ultra marathon stretching from the north to the south.
Truganini, a famous nineteenth-century Aboriginal Tasmanian woman, was born on Bruny Island around 1812.
The island boasts some of Australia's highest sea cliffs made of dramatic columnar dolerite rocks.
Bruny Island serves as a critical breeding sanctuary for the endangered swift parrot each spring.
Visitors reach the island via a short ferry ride across the D'Entrecasteaux Channel from Kettering.
Captain James Cook anchored in Adventure Bay in 1777 during his third voyage of discovery.
Captain William Bligh planted Tasmania's very first apple trees at Adventure Bay in 1788.
Australian fur seals frequently haul out and lounge along the rugged coastline of the southern park.
The island hosts Australia's southernmost boutique whisky distillery producing handcrafted single malt spirits.
Clambering up the timber stairs at The Neck Lookout rewards you with sweeping panoramic ocean views.
Prevailing Roaring Forties winds bring some of the cleanest, freshest air in the world to Bruny.
